title: Register mcp__opum-quest__dashboard and route /quest to it through the skill, now that the slash command is gone
description:
Two rulings meet here, both 2026-10-03.

seq 174 (opum-doc#629, pane-dashboard-tool-design.md, main dfde45e; recorded on opum-agent OPAG-1089). Operator's words, verbatim: "Yes per-plugin. Do you agree with this design?" Design, by opum-doc: each pane mod registers a dashboard tool Claude can call, so the plugin's own skill opens the pane for "quest dashboard" and sends everything else to the CLI.

seq 176 (ODOC-OP-2026-10-03-07, recorded on opum-agent OPAG-1089 at origin/dev 688d78ff), decided after the QCLI-440 clash check confirmed that a command named `quest` is REFUSED by the engine because the plugin's own skill owns /opum-quest:quest. Its text for quest-cli, verbatim: "the `quest` skill routes `dashboard`, `board`, `full`, `fleet` and `local` to `mcp__opum-quest__dashboard` (scope and full arguments); every other argument goes to the CLI."

So this task is the board's new way in: the tool, plus the skill that routes to it, now that the slash command is gone (QCLI-440).

Design points that bind:
- The tool is `mcp__opum-quest__dashboard`, registered at session.start, served by a `tool.call` hook. Inputs, all optional: `scope` (fleet|local), `full` (boolean), `task` (a task id to open in the detail view).
- It NEVER takes the keyboard: it opens the pane without `focus`, because Claude may call it unasked and the person may be typing. Same rule as a restored full-mode pane.
- The description stays to one or two sentences -- it is listed to Claude in every session that loads the mod.
- An unknown task id returns an error result naming it and does not open on something else instead.
- The skill file is GENERATED (QCLI-372), so the routing verb goes into the generator in src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts, not into skills/quest/SKILL.md by hand.
- Fallback where mods are unavailable -- Claude Code older than 2.1.287, a `claude -p` run, or mods turned off: say the pane is unavailable here and answer from the CLI instead.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The mod registers mcp__opum-quest__dashboard at session start, with a one- or two-sentence description
Calling the tool opens the board WITHOUT focus, applying scope (fleet|local), full mode, and selecting the named task when one is given
An unknown task id returns an error result naming it, and opens nothing else instead

The generated quest skill routes a request whose first word is `dashboard` -- with `full`, `fleet`, `local` or a task id combining after it -- to the tool in one call, and every other argument to the CLI (including "quest board", which the CLI already serves), with the CLI fallback where mods are unavailable. Read at skills/quest/SKILL.md:17-22
Tests cover registration, each input, the unknown-id error and the no-focus rule, and run on the terminal and desktop surfaces

plan: 1. Remove the quest-board slash command registration and its command.run hook from hooks/register.tsx, keeping setScope/setFull/setCollapsed/setReadRefs for their remaining key and button callers.

2. Register mcp__opum-quest__dashboard at session.start (one-sentence description, optional scope/full/task schema) and serve it from a tool.call hook: apply scope and full, select a named task, open the pane unfocused, error on an unknown task id.
3. Teach questSkillDoc in src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts the dashboard routing and CLI fallback, then regenerate skills/quest/SKILL.md with scripts/plugin-skill.mjs --write.

4. Add tests/board.test.tsx coverage for registration, the no-focus open, each input, and the unknown-id error, on terminal and desktop, and confirm each new behaviour test fails against the pre-change code.
5. Record the change under CHANGELOG.md Unreleased.
6. Run test:mod, typecheck, lint, format:check, layer:check and npm test.
implementationNotes: Removed the boards slash command and its command.run hook. The mod registers mcp__opum-quest__dashboard at session.start and serves it from a tool.call hook taking optional scope (fleet|local), full (boolean) and task (a task id); it applies them and then opens the pane WITHOUT focus, because Claude may call it unasked while the person is typing. An unknown task id is resolved by one task view per workspace on the board -- the rows cannot answer it, being read at one status filter and one scope -- and comes back as an error result naming it with nothing opened. The result is one line: Opened the Quest board, fleet scope, OCLI-8 selected.

Routing superseded mid-task by opum-doc seq 180: there is no bare full, fleet, local, board or pane verb. The generated skill is now a prefix test -- quest dashboard with full, fleet, local or a task id after it is ONE tool call; every argument that does not start at dashboard goes to the CLI. AC3s text still names the revoked verb table, so it is left unchecked here pending an amendment. Parsing conflict checked and reported, not fixed: the CLI has a real board command (src/application/command-help.ts:531) and no dashboard command; quest board exits 0, quest board full exits 2 (board accepts only --json and --plain), quest dashboard exits 2 (Unknown or missing Quest command). The prefix is therefore unambiguous, and quest board full is a visible usage error rather than a wrong pane.

Evidence: five new engine tests in tests/board.test.tsx, each looping terminal and desktop. All five fail against the pre-change hooks module (22 pass / 5 fail). Three mutations redden a predicted subset with the rest green: forcing focus on the tools open (no-focus test red), dropping the setFullState call (full test red only), dropping the setScope call (scope test red only), and short-circuiting the findTask probe (unknown-id test red only). Gates: test:mod 27 pass / 0 fail; typecheck 0; lint 0; format:check 0; layer:check 0; npm test 1081 pass / 1 fail, the known bun-pin test (machine bun 1.3.14 against the repos 1.4.2 pin).
